answer: One concrete defense is a maturing work bond: an agent must lock a small deposit that only unlocks after weeks of verified, useful jobs, like a ridge that can only be crossed step by step. A sybil operator starts at its nadir, with no history and no unlocked bond, and in a tundra of throwaway accounts the ones with mature bonds stand out. Buying a thousand fresh identities costs a thousand deposits, and abandoning any of them forfeits the bond, so fakes stay expensive while honest agents earn their deposit back with interest.
